english: Let $E$ be the locus of the complex numbers $z$ satisfying $|z-3-4i|+|z+3+4i|=20$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Let the latus rectum of $E$ through the focus $3+4i$ have the end points $P$ and $Q$, representing the complex numbers $p$ and $q$. Then the value of $\mathrm{Re}(p)\cdot\mathrm{Re}(q)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $E$ उन सम्मिश्र संख्याओं $z$ का बिन्दुपथ है जो $|z-3-4i|+|z+3+4i|=20$ को संतुष्ट करती हैं, जहाँ $i=\sqrt{-1}$ है। माना कि नाभि $3+4i$ से होकर जाने वाले $E$ के नाभिलम्ब के अन्त्य बिन्दु $P$ तथा $Q$ हैं, जो सम्मिश्र संख्याओं $p$ तथा $q$ को निरूपित करते हैं। तब $\mathrm{Re}(p)\cdot\mathrm{Re}(q)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Major axis along $u=\dfrac{3+4i}{5}$; the latus rectum through $3+4i$ is perpendicular to it, along $iu=\dfrac{-4+3i}{5}$, with semi-length $\dfrac{b^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{15}{2}$
solution_full: The sum of distances from the fixed points $S_{1}=3+4i$ and $S_{2}=-3-4i$ is $20>|S_{1}-S_{2}|=10$, so $E$ is an ellipse with foci $S_{1},S_{2}$, centre $0$, $2a=20$, $2c=10$.
So $a=10$, $c=5$, $b^{2}=a^{2}-c^{2}=75$, $e=\dfrac{1}{2}$. The major axis is along the unit vector $u=\dfrac{3+4i}{5}$.

The latus rectum through $S_{1}$ is the chord through $S_{1}$ perpendicular to the major axis, i.e. along $iu=\dfrac{-4+3i}{5}$ (multiplication by $i$ turns through $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$). Its half-length is $\dfrac{b^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{75}{10}=\dfrac{15}{2}$.

(Alternatively: at an end of the latus rectum the two focal distances are $\dfrac{b^{2}}{a}=7.5$ and $2a-7.5=12.5$, and $7.5^{2}+10^{2}=12.5^{2}$, consistent with the right angle at the focus $S_{1}$.)
originality_note: New: an ellipse given by a complex focal-sum locus with an oblique axis; the latus rectum end points are found by turning the axis direction through pi/2 (multiplication by i) and using b^2/a (way 5). Closest known: ends of the latus rectum of x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1. Different because: the axis is oblique, so the student must work with the direction (3+4i)/5 and its rotation instead of standard coordinates.

key_step: Get a, c, b^2 from the focal-sum locus, then place the latus rectum through 3+4i along i(3+4i)/5 with half-length b^2/a.
